Package ca.refundr.highspring.database.scope

Class TestDatabaseScope

java.lang.Object
ca.refundr.highspring.database.scope.TestDatabaseScope
All Implemented Interfaces:
DatabaseScope, AutoCloseable
public final class TestDatabaseScope extends Object implements DatabaseScope
Isolated Postgres database for one automated test: create → migrate → use → drop.

Why this is good database-test practice

  • Isolation — Each instance gets its own database name ({main}_test0, {main}_test1, …). Tests never share rows, so order of execution does not matter and parallel runs do not collide.
  • Real schema — Flyway applies the same migration scripts as production (MainDatabaseScope). You are not testing against a hand-built mock schema that can drift from what ships.
  • Clean teardown — close() drops the database. Leftover data cannot poison the next run or the developer’s main DATABASE_URL database.
  • Same interface as production — Implements DatabaseScope, so app code under test sees the same transaction(…) / getDataSource() API as the live server. Swapping test vs main is a constructor choice, not a fork of business logic.
  • Conservative pool — Small Hikari pool (MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_TEST), autoCommit=false, and READ_COMMITTED match how the app expects to use connections, without exhausting Postgres slots when many tests spin up.
  • Admin connection separate from app pool — CREATE/DROP DATABASE run against the postgres system database with a short-lived datasource. That is required (you cannot drop the DB you are connected to) and keeps DDL out of the application connection pool.
  • Fast enough per test — Creating an empty Postgres database and running a small Flyway set is typically a second or two locally. That is cheap compared with debugging flaky shared-DB tests, and still much lighter than starting Docker for every class. The tiny Hikari pool and dropping the whole DB (no per-table cleanup loops) keep setup/teardown simple and quick.

Why this pattern is easy to reuse in other repos

  • It depends only on config keys (DATABASE_URL, username, password) and classpath Flyway locations — no Highspring domain types.
  • The lifecycle is copy-friendly: parse JDBC URL → derive test name → create DB → migrate → expose DataSource → on close, drop DB. Other services can lift the class (or the idea) with a different migration package path.
  • Pairing it with AutoCloseable / try-with-resources (try (TestDatabaseScope db = new TestDatabaseScope(config))) is a standard Java idiom every repo already understands.
  • Prefer this over “truncate all tables between tests” when schemas grow: dropping the database resets extensions, sequences, and Flyway history in one shot.

Requires a local Postgres that allows CREATE DATABASE (typical for DBngin / Docker CI). The main app database named in DATABASE_URL is never truncated; only sibling *_testN databases are created and destroyed.
